newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil posts $853 million November trade deficit.
newsitem.headline: Brazil posts $853 million November trade deficit.

text.p: Brazil posted an $853 million trade deficit in November, with exports totalling $3.912 billion and imports at $4.765 billion, the Ministry of Industry and Commerce said Monday.
The ministry said November results brought the year-to-date trade deficit to $3.754 billion, versus a deficit of $3.3 billion in the January-November period of 1995.
In November 1995, Brazil posted a $15 million trade surplus, with exports of $4.048 billion and imports of $4.033 billion.
The November result was in line with market expectations and was considerably lower than October 1996's record $1.308 billion trade gap.
The ministry attributed November's improvement to a 2.73 percent increase in the daily average value of exports, which rose to $195.6 million from $190.4 million in October.
It also said average daily imports of $238.3 million in November were 4.6 percent lower than the $249.8 million average in October.
The ministry said exports of primary commodities in November totaled $982 million, 25.1 percent of the total, versus commodity exports of $845 million, or 20.8 percent of the total, in November 1995.
Semi-manufactured exports in November were $671 million, 17.15 percent of total exports, compared with $882 million, or 21.79 percent, in November 1995.
Manufactured goods totaled $2.186 billion, or 55.88 percent of the total in November, against $2.260 billion, or 55.83 percent, in November 1995.
